evidence_records.Full citation: Zhao, Zhilong, and Yindi Liu. 2025. A Confidence–Diversity Framework for Calibrating AI Judgement in Accessible Qualitative Coding Tasks. arXiv:2508.02029v2.
evidence_records.Title: A Confidence–Diversity Framework for Calibrating AI Judgement in Accessible Qualitative Coding Tasks
evidence_records.Authors: Zhilong Zhao; Yindi Liu
evidence_records.Peer-reviewed status: not peer reviewed / peer review not verified
evidence_records.Publication history notes: arXiv v2 dated 16 August 2025
evidence_records.Citation count, source, and retrieval da: not collected; official arXiv full text inspected 2026-08-24
evidence_records.Relationship/dependence family: confidence/diversity calibration and selective human-review workflow
evidence_records.Research objective: Test whether model self-confidence plus inter-model vote diversity can predict coding agreement and allocate human review in accessible fixed-code tasks.
evidence_records.Claimed qualitative methodology: deductive qualitative content coding with human–AI adjudication
evidence_records.Actual operationalized methodology: Eight LLM variants make 710 binary segment–category judgments, report confidence, and are ensembled; normalized Shannon vote entropy and confidence feed a risk score that routes cases to auto-accept/light/full review, followed by stratified expert audit and six-dataset validation.
evidence_records.Inductive, deductive, or hybrid: deductive
evidence_records.Domain: academic-identity interviews plus finance, medicine, law and benchmark text classification
evidence_records.Dataset name: 71 academic-identity interview segments; Finance-News600, PubMed-RCT600, ECHR-A, Moral-Stories, WMT20 QE, XNLI-zh
evidence_records.Public or restricted data: anonymized interview subset and public external datasets released; full identifiable corpus restricted
evidence_records.Number of documents: 71 primary interview segments plus six 600-item/public benchmark subsets
evidence_records.Number of participants: 4 adult interview participants in the primary corpus
evidence_records.Approximate corpus size: 710 primary segment–code units / 5,680 model decisions; 1,242 audit judgments reported; six external datasets
evidence_records.Document length: short interview segments and benchmark instances
evidence_records.Language: primary corpus not explicitly stated; external set includes English and Chinese
evidence_records.Sensitive-data status: identifiable interview corpus restricted under IRB; anonymized replication subset released
evidence_records.Exact model/version: Claude 3.5 and 3.7 Sonnet; GPT-4o and o3-mini; Gemini 2.5 Flash; DeepSeek V3 and Reasoner; release-date labels in paper are not all conventional snapshot IDs
evidence_records.Prompting strategy: single-response and chain-of-thought variants; binary decision plus 1–5 self-confidence; category definition and decision rule; temperature .2/.4
evidence_records.Agent roles: models vote and self-report confidence; risk model routes cases; experts adjudicate selected items
evidence_records.Human role: two research assistants provide baseline; three qualitative researchers blind-code the audit; two senior qualitative scholars adjudicate no-majority cases
evidence_records.Generated outputs: binary codes, confidence, rationales, diversity/risk scores, review tiers and adjudicated labels
evidence_records.Evidence/provenance mechanism: every request/response logged; labels tie to source segment/category; public raw outputs and prompts
evidence_records.Baselines: two-human coding; confidence-only regression; eight-model majority; alternative weights; six external datasets
evidence_records.Number of runs or seeds: random seed 42 reported; 10-fold cross-validation and 1,000 bootstrap resamples; one logged response per stated model/configuration
evidence_records.Automatic metrics: accuracy, error rate, Cohen's kappa, Pearson r, R², MAE, normalized Shannon entropy, precision, recall, F1
evidence_records.Human-evaluation design: 20% stratified audit by review tier with three blinded researchers and senior adjudication
evidence_records.Number and expertise of evaluators: two baseline research assistants; three trained qualitative researchers; two senior qualitative-methodology scholars
evidence_records.Inter-rater reliability: two-human baseline κ=.67; three-researcher audit κ=.82; model majority κ=.89; triaged workflow κ=.93
evidence_records.Statistical analysis: OLS, nested 10-fold CV, Pearson correlation, 1,000-fold bootstrap, two-sided tests with Benjamini–Hochberg correction, power analysis
evidence_records.Principal results: Confidence correlated with agreement (r=.82); confidence plus diversity yielded category-level R²=.979. Auto-accept covered 35% with under 5% error and the workflow reported 65% less manual review. External κ gains ranged .20–.78, but tasks were explicitly easy for current LLMs.
evidence_records.Efficiency or cost results: reported 65% reduction in manual review; compute/API cost not reported
evidence_records.Ethics and privacy treatment: SCUT IRB approvals 2024-Q-017/SCUTXWWX230057 and written consent; identifiable corpus restricted; bias, drift and independent audit discussed
evidence_records.Reproducibility resources: Harvard Dataverse DOI 10.7910/DVN/G1AYGK with prompts, JSON payloads, outputs, scripts, notebooks, figures and anonymized data subset
evidence_records.Author-reported limitations: small primary sample, only ten categories, reduced diversity resolution for small panels, accessible-task ceiling effects, no validation on highly interpretive long-context tasks
evidence_records.Additional validity concerns: Agreement is predicted partly from vote diversity itself and is not interpretive validity; the striking R² uses ten category-level observations, and claims about exceeding human cognition go beyond the accessible-task evidence.
evidence_records.Relationship to prior papers: Methodological extension of ensemble uncertainty and selective review to qualitative coding.
evidence_records.Relevance to the proposed ARR project: Potentially changes the ARR evaluation ranking: include confidence/diversity triage, but require hard-task, held-out and plurality-sensitive validation before treating it as reliable.

evidence_records.Full citation: Xu, Qidi, Nuzha Amjad, Grace Giles, Alexa Cumming, De'angelo Hermesky, Alexander Wen, Min Ji Kwak, and Yejin Kim. 2025. A Multi-Agent Large Language Model Framework for Automated Qualitative Analysis. arXiv:2512.16063v1.
evidence_records.Title: A Multi-Agent Large Language Model Framework for Automated Qualitative Analysis
evidence_records.Authors: Qidi Xu; Nuzha Amjad; Grace Giles; Alexa Cumming; De'angelo Hermesky; Alexander Wen; Min Ji Kwak; Yejin Kim
evidence_records.Peer-reviewed status: not peer reviewed / peer review not verified
evidence_records.Publication history notes: arXiv preprint; no peer-reviewed venue verified in inspected text
evidence_records.Citation count, source, and retrieval da: not collected; official arXiv full text inspected 2026-08-24
evidence_records.Relationship/dependence family: CoTI system; distinct from other multi-agent thematic-analysis frameworks
evidence_records.Research objective: Automate clue extraction, transcript-level theme generation and cross-transcript codebook development, and test junior-investigator interaction/automation bias.
evidence_records.Claimed qualitative methodology: inductive thematic analysis
evidence_records.Actual operationalized methodology: A QwQ-32B Instructor uses four internal roles to refine evidence/reasoning prompts; GPT-4o-mini Thematizer runs three times per transcript and unions outputs; GPT-4o-mini CodebookGenerator clusters themes; outputs are compared to one senior investigator and four junior investigators.
evidence_records.Inductive, deductive, or hybrid: inductive, objective-specific
evidence_records.Domain: heart-failure medication experience; external Sierra Leone COVID-19 health-system corpus
evidence_records.Dataset name: 12 heart-failure patient interviews; 21 external COVID-19 interviews
evidence_records.Public or restricted data: heart-failure transcripts restricted; external COVID corpus public
evidence_records.Number of participants: 12 heart-failure patients; four junior-investigator users; external participant count not extracted
evidence_records.Approximate corpus size: 33 interview transcripts across primary and external checks
evidence_records.Sensitive-data status: clinical patient interviews; deidentified and not publicly released
evidence_records.Exact model/version: QwQ-32B; GPT-4o-mini; Whisper small; text-embedding-3-small
evidence_records.Prompting strategy: objective-specific iterative clue/reasoning prompt optimization; direct-quote constraints; three-run union; interactive retry/feedback UI
evidence_records.Agent roles: Instructor comprises clue, reasoning, evaluation and optimization roles; Thematizer extracts clues/reasoning/themes; CodebookGenerator merges themes
evidence_records.Human role: senior investigator supplies reference analysis; four junior medical investigators manually analyze then use UI; researchers verify prompts, themes and codebook
evidence_records.Unit of analysis: interview, direct-quote clue, theme and cross-interview code
evidence_records.Generated outputs: clues, reasoning chains, themes, structured codebook and user-refined outputs
evidence_records.Evidence/provenance mechanism: direct quotes are required and retained with themes; codebook contains original themes and representative clues; UI supports source search
evidence_records.Baselines: senior investigator, four junior investigators, QwQ-32B basic LLM, GPT-4o-mini ablations, LDA, Top2Vec and BERTopic
evidence_records.Number of runs or seeds: three Thematizer runs unioned; one basic-QwQ run; two interviews used for instruction development; no stochastic seeds
evidence_records.Automatic metrics: clue Jaccard/precision/recall/F1; theme/codebook embedding cosine similarity; ablations and response time
evidence_records.Human-evaluation design: senior investigator reference; four juniors manually analyze assigned interviews, interact with CoTI, and complete QUEST-informed survey
evidence_records.Number and expertise of evaluators: one senior investigator; four medical-school junior investigators; research team
evidence_records.Inter-rater reliability: not reported; evaluation uses similarity to one senior reference
evidence_records.Statistical analysis: descriptive comparisons/ablations; inferential testing not reported
evidence_records.Principal results: CoTI clue Jaccard=.403, precision=.550, recall=.630, F1=.569; theme cosine=.431 and codebook cosine=.621. It beat basic QwQ and topic models, while junior feedback yielded only marginal gains and suggested automation bias.
evidence_records.Efficiency or cost results: about 1 minute/interview for CoTI versus 3 minutes for basic QwQ; about 10 seconds versus 2 minutes for codebook generation
evidence_records.Ethics and privacy treatment: UT IRB protocols HSC-MS-21-0874 and HSC-SBMI-13-0549 stated; heart-failure data restricted; participant privacy and conflicts disclosed
evidence_records.Reproducibility resources: GitHub https://github.com/QidiXu96/CoTI-MultiAgent-Theme-Analysis; full prompts in supplement; external data at OSF; clinical transcripts unavailable
evidence_records.Author-reported limitations: 12-interview single primary case, only four juniors, no senior-feedback condition and limited cross-context validation
evidence_records.Additional validity concerns: A single senior analysis is not ground truth; embedding similarity rewards lexical/semantic resemblance rather than interpretive quality, and unioning runs structurally favors recall.
evidence_records.Relationship to prior papers: Uses interview data from an earlier clinical study and explicitly compares with TAMA, Auto-TA and Thematic-LM; no duplicate publication detected.
evidence_records.Relevance to the proposed ARR project: Material RQ1/RQ4/RQ5 evidence: prioritize quote provenance and automation-bias tests; score lower than systems with independent plural human references.

evidence_records.Full citation: Flaherty, Leah Russell, and Kendra H. Oliver. 2025. A Positive Spin: Large Language Models Can Help Directors Evaluate Programs Through Their Patients' Own Words. Pain Reports 10(1):e1219. https://doi.org/10.1097/PR9.0000000000001219.
evidence_records.Title: A Positive Spin: Large Language Models Can Help Directors Evaluate Programs Through Their Patients' Own Words
evidence_records.Authors: Leah Russell Flaherty; Kendra H. Oliver
evidence_records.Publication history notes: received 25 June 2024; accepted 30 October 2024; published online 24 December 2024; 2025 issue/collection; CC BY 4.0
evidence_records.Citation count, source, and retrieval da: not collected; full PMC article inspected 2026-08-24
evidence_records.Relationship/dependence family: applied ChatGPT-assisted program-evaluation case study
evidence_records.Research objective: Demonstrate a feasible low-resource LLM-assisted thematic review of pain-program open-ended feedback.
evidence_records.Claimed qualitative methodology: inductive thematic analysis
evidence_records.Actual operationalized methodology: All responses are sent once through a staged GPT-4 prompt for detailed open codes and example quotes; one researcher manually reviews/organizes codes into seven themes with model assistance, and two researchers check the final output for fit/hallucination.
evidence_records.Inductive, deductive, or hybrid: inductive with manual theme organization
evidence_records.Dataset name: Empowered Relief postclass satisfaction survey
evidence_records.Public or restricted data: restricted/deidentified
evidence_records.Number of documents: 82 responses to one open-ended survey question
evidence_records.Approximate corpus size: 82 short open-ended responses
evidence_records.Sensitive-data status: patient feedback; deidentified before upload and identifying/proprietary details removed
evidence_records.Exact model/version: paid ChatGPT GPT-4; snapshot not reported
evidence_records.Prompting strategy: detailed/open-code instruction, at least five example quotes per code, and repeated request for more codes at least twice
evidence_records.Single-agent or multi-agent: single chat model plus human review
evidence_records.Agent roles: ChatGPT proposes codes and illustrative quotations
evidence_records.Human role: R1 engineers prompts, manually evaluates codes and organizes themes; R1/R2 review final outputs for thematic fit and hallucination
evidence_records.Generated outputs: at least 15 codes, seven broad themes and supporting quotations
evidence_records.Evidence/provenance mechanism: the prompt requires five exact sample quotes per code; full exchange and supplement are linked
evidence_records.Baselines: no independent human-only or model baseline
evidence_records.Number of runs or seeds: one chat workflow with at least two follow-up generations; no independent replicate
evidence_records.Automatic metrics: none
evidence_records.Human-evaluation design: two authors manually checked all reported codes/themes and quotes; no blinded or independent evaluation
evidence_records.Number and expertise of evaluators: two authors, including pain-program and responsible-data-science expertise
evidence_records.Inter-rater reliability: not reported
evidence_records.Statistical analysis: none for coding validity
evidence_records.Principal results: Seven themes were produced; manual review found four example quotes that did not clearly fit their assigned theme but no fabricated quotes.
evidence_records.Efficiency or cost results: described as ergonomic/time-saving; no measured time or cost
evidence_records.Ethics and privacy treatment: Allegheny Singer Research Institute designated project 2022-239 QA/QI; deidentification and cloud-data/privacy risks are explicitly discussed
evidence_records.Reproducibility resources: full shared ChatGPT exchange and supplementary theme table; raw patient responses not released; model snapshot absent
evidence_records.Author-reported limitations: LLMs tend toward description rather than interpretation, are opaque, require validation and prompt skill, and can create privacy risks
evidence_records.Additional validity concerns: No human-only comparator, no repeated runs, no reliability metric and author-only checking; claims about bias mitigation or unexpected insight are not causally established.
evidence_records.Relationship to prior papers: Applied program-evaluation use case rather than a system benchmark.
evidence_records.Relevance to the proposed ARR project: Low-ranked evidence for performance but strong illustrative case for quote verification, disclosure, privacy, and separating speed claims from validity.

evidence_records.Full citation: Yue, Yongjie, Dong Liu, Yilin Lv, Junyi Hao, and Peixuan Cui. 2025. A Practical Guide and Assessment on Using ChatGPT to Conduct Grounded Theory: Tutorial. Journal of Medical Internet Research 27:e70122. https://doi.org/10.2196/70122.
evidence_records.Title: A Practical Guide and Assessment on Using ChatGPT to Conduct Grounded Theory: Tutorial
evidence_records.Authors: Yongjie Yue; Dong Liu; Yilin Lv; Junyi Hao; Peixuan Cui
evidence_records.Publication history notes: received 16 December 2024; accepted 15 April 2025; published 14 May 2025; CC BY
evidence_records.Citation count, source, and retrieval da: not collected; full PMC article and appendices inspected 2026-08-24
evidence_records.Relationship/dependence family: manual-NVivo versus ChatGPT grounded-theory comparison
evidence_records.Research objective: Provide a reproducible three-stage ChatGPT grounded-theory tutorial and compare its coding with independent NVivo-assisted manual analysis.
evidence_records.Claimed qualitative methodology: grounded theory: open, axial and selective coding
evidence_records.Actual operationalized methodology: Two researchers manually code in NVivo; a separate researcher feeds eight Chinese transcripts to ChatGPT 4-Turbo in chunks and iteratively requests open, clustered/axial and selective codes, with manual screening/refinement; an expert plus two researchers semantically align outputs before computing agreement.
evidence_records.Inductive, deductive, or hybrid: inductive
evidence_records.Domain: blind gamers' experiences in a Chinese MMORPG
evidence_records.Dataset name: Listen and Play in Jianghu interview corpus
evidence_records.Public or restricted data: restricted/anonymized
evidence_records.Approximate corpus size: approximately 40,000 Chinese words/characters as reported
evidence_records.Document length: semi-structured interviews; some split because of context limits
evidence_records.Sensitive-data status: interviews with blind participants; anonymized and ethics-approved
evidence_records.Exact model/version: ChatGPT 4-Turbo; snapshot not reported; paper states an 8,192-token context
evidence_records.Prompting strategy: role prompt, iterative open coding with source alignment, repeated depth requests, paired-transcript axial clustering, and selective-code relationship prompts
evidence_records.Single-agent or multi-agent: single model with extensive human iteration
evidence_records.Agent roles: ChatGPT proposes codes, clusters/categories, core category and theory relationships
evidence_records.Human role: two independent manual coders create comparison analysis; another researcher operates ChatGPT; one expert and two researchers semantically align codes; humans refine every AI stage and return to source interviews
evidence_records.Unit of analysis: text segment, open-code node/reference point, axial category and selective/core category
evidence_records.Generated outputs: 274 open codes, seven main categories, a core category and preliminary theoretical framework
evidence_records.Evidence/provenance mechanism: open-code prompts require exact source statements; appendices provide full coding outputs, theory diagrams and generic prompts
evidence_records.Baselines: two-researcher NVivo manual grounded-theory analysis
evidence_records.Number of runs or seeds: repeated conversational queries but no independent stochastic replications
evidence_records.Automatic metrics: node/reference/coverage counts, percent agreement, Cohen's kappa distributions and t tests
evidence_records.Human-evaluation design: one domain expert and two researchers inspect semantic equivalence of 274 AI and 289 manual open codes and compare axial/selective relationships
evidence_records.Number and expertise of evaluators: two manual researchers, one ChatGPT-operating researcher, one domain expert and two semantic-alignment reviewers, with some role overlap
evidence_records.Inter-rater reliability: manual coders reached more than 85% before full coding; raw human–AI agreement exceeded 95% largely because most text was uncoded, while the largest κ category was only slight agreement
evidence_records.Statistical analysis: SPSS t tests for node/reference/coverage differences; descriptive κ distributions
evidence_records.Principal results: Manual and AI counts did not significantly differ, but ChatGPT had weaker depth, context, connection and organization. Manual analysis made eight categories versus seven AI categories; core narratives overlapped after human reconstruction.
evidence_records.Efficiency or cost results: manual NVivo analysis took three weeks for two researchers; ChatGPT analysis took one day after prompts were finalized
evidence_records.Ethics and privacy treatment: Renmin University ethics approval 20220028; informed consent, withdrawal right, anonymization and 50 RMB compensation; privacy/bias risks discussed
evidence_records.Reproducibility resources: OA full article; appendices contain workflows, complete coding results, theory and prompts; interview corpus not released and model snapshot absent
evidence_records.Author-reported limitations: eight participants, one Chinese context, one model, instability/bias and need for multi-model/longitudinal replication
evidence_records.Additional validity concerns: Semantic alignment was performed before agreement computation and high raw agreement was inflated by uncoded text; grounded theory relies heavily on human screening/reconstruction, so the study does not show autonomous theory generation.
evidence_records.Relationship to prior papers: Empirical tutorial extending earlier ChatGPT thematic/grounded-theory case studies.
evidence_records.Relevance to the proposed ARR project: Material RQ2/RQ5 evidence for explicit claimed-versus-operationalized coding, source-linked comparisons, manual reconstruction and prevalence-aware agreement reporting.

evidence_records.Full citation: Ahtisham, Bakhtawar, Kirk Vanacore, Jinsook Lee, Zhuqian Zhou, Doug Pietrzak, and Rene F. Kizilcec. 2026. AI Annotation Orchestration: Evaluating LLM Verifiers to Improve the Quality of LLM Annotations in Learning Analytics. LAK 2026. https://doi.org/10.1145/3785022.3785095.
evidence_records.Title: AI Annotation Orchestration: Evaluating LLM Verifiers to Improve the Quality of LLM Annotations in Learning Analytics
evidence_records.Authors: Bakhtawar Ahtisham; Kirk Vanacore; Jinsook Lee; Zhuqian Zhou; Doug Pietrzak; Rene F. Kizilcec
evidence_records.Venue: 16th International Learning Analytics and Knowledge Conference (LAK 2026)
evidence_records.Publication history notes: screened from 2025 arXiv:2511.09785v2; inspected text is the LAK 2026 proceedings version with DOI and April–May 2026 venue dates
evidence_records.Citation count, source, and retrieval da: not collected; official arXiv-hosted proceedings text inspected 2026-08-24
evidence_records.Relationship/dependence family: 2025 preprint / 2026 peer-reviewed version family; verifier-orchestration study
evidence_records.Research objective: Compare unverified, self-verified and every directional cross-verified combination of three LLMs for qualitative tutoring-move annotation.
evidence_records.Claimed qualitative methodology: inductive–deductive qualitative codebook development followed by deductive tutor-move coding
evidence_records.Actual operationalized methodology: A human develops/refines an 11-class single-best-fit rubric; author–Gemini agreement plus blinded human adjudication creates the reference; GPT-5, Claude 3 Sonnet and Gemini 2.5 Flash annotate each tutor utterance, then self- or cross-verify against the same rubric.
evidence_records.Inductive, deductive, or hybrid: hybrid codebook development, then deductive coding
evidence_records.Dataset name: pseudonymized UPchieve text-chat tutoring sessions
evidence_records.Public or restricted data: deidentified; public-release status not reported
evidence_records.Number of participants: not reported
evidence_records.Approximate corpus size: 1,881 utterances; 501 initial author–Gemini disagreements
evidence_records.Document length: session chunks with median about 80 turns and 1–2-turn overlap
evidence_records.Sensitive-data status: student/tutor interaction; deidentified
evidence_records.Exact model/version: GPT-5; Claude 3 Sonnet; Gemini 2.5 Flash; provider snapshot IDs not reported
evidence_records.Prompting strategy: same rubric-grounded prompt with definitions/concise examples; focal tutor utterance plus preceding student and prior tutor turn; verifier sees initial label/rationale and retains or revises
evidence_records.Agent roles: base model assigns one move and rationale; same/different model audits against rubric
evidence_records.Human role: Author 1 manually codes and builds codebook; external experienced tutoring reviewer blindly adjudicates author–Gemini disagreements; humans remain proposed edge-case adjudicators
evidence_records.Generated outputs: single tutor-move label, rationale, verification decision and final label
evidence_records.Evidence/provenance mechanism: logs initial label, verification decision, final label and rubric-grounded justification; source turn context retained
evidence_records.Baselines: three unverified models; self-verification; all six directional cross-verifier pairs; human–Gemini adjudicated reference
evidence_records.Number of runs or seeds: one pass per orchestration configuration; no stochastic replication/seeds reported
evidence_records.Automatic metrics: per-code Cohen's kappa and delta-kappa
evidence_records.Human-evaluation design: blinded disagreement-focused external adjudication of 501 human–Gemini disagreements
evidence_records.Number and expertise of evaluators: one author coder/codebook developer and one external reviewer experienced in human tutoring implementation/research
evidence_records.Inter-rater reliability: unverified mean κ=.32; self-verification mean .64; cross-verification mean .44; verified overall mean .51
evidence_records.Statistical analysis: descriptive per-construct/per-pair kappa comparisons; no uncertainty intervals/significance tests reported
evidence_records.Principal results: Self-verification almost doubled mean κ and improved every model; cross-verification averaged +37% but was directional and sometimes harmful. Intent-heavy Prompting/Revoicing remained hard.
evidence_records.Efficiency or cost results: described as scalable/low-cost but compute cost and latency were not optimized or reported
evidence_records.Ethics and privacy treatment: data are described as deidentified/pseudonymized; IRB, consent, access and fairness analysis are not reported in the inspected paper
evidence_records.Reproducibility resources: full rubric reportedly in supplements; no verified public data/code/prompts repository or provider snapshot IDs
evidence_records.Author-reported limitations: 30 sessions, one math domain, text-only, one rubric/prompt family, single-label assumption, model updates and unmeasured compute/latency
evidence_records.Additional validity concerns: Reference labels partly inherit Gemini: all human–Gemini agreements are accepted and only disagreements are independently reviewed, creating possible correlated-model bias; no repeated runs establish stability.
evidence_records.Relationship to prior papers: The 2025 arXiv record and 2026 LAK DOI are one version family and must be counted once.
evidence_records.Relevance to the proposed ARR project: Material RQ3/RQ5 evidence: self-verification rises in ranking, but cross-verifier direction must be tuned and a fully independent human reference remains mandatory.

evidence_records.Full citation: Flanders, Samuel, Melati Nungsari, and Mark Cheong Wing Loong. 2025. AI Coding with Few-Shot Prompting for Thematic Analysis. arXiv:2504.07408v1.
evidence_records.Title: AI Coding with Few-Shot Prompting for Thematic Analysis
evidence_records.Authors: Samuel Flanders; Melati Nungsari; Mark Cheong Wing Loong
evidence_records.Peer-reviewed status: not peer reviewed / peer review not verified
evidence_records.Publication history notes: arXiv v1 submitted 10 April 2025
evidence_records.Citation count, source, and retrieval da: not collected; official arXiv PDF inspected 2026-08-24
evidence_records.Relationship/dependence family: Socratic/few-shot LLM thematic-coding workflow
evidence_records.Research objective: Improve passage-level AI thematic codes with error-driven prompt iteration and semantically matched few-shot examples.
evidence_records.Claimed qualitative methodology: coding for thematic analysis in a coding-reliability/positivist framing
evidence_records.Actual operationalized methodology: GPT-3.5 Turbo summarizes 2,530 news articles and labels passages; Ada embeddings, UMAP/HDBSCAN and later k-means form semantic clusters; a long Socratic pipeline generates cluster exemplars; final few-shot prompts code theme, speaker/target and valence; three reviewers iteratively validate a fixed sample.
evidence_records.Inductive, deductive, or hybrid: hybrid: LLM-inductive exemplar/code generation followed by prompt-guided passage coding
evidence_records.Dataset name: 2,530 Malaysian news articles from five outlets, 2017–2023
evidence_records.Public or restricted data: source articles public; compiled corpus/review sheets not clearly archived at a working URL
evidence_records.Number of participants: not applicable; three human reviewers
evidence_records.Approximate corpus size: 2,530 articles segmented at line breaks; 414 passages in fixed human-review sample
evidence_records.Document length: articles summarized; passages shorter than 50 characters initially dropped and stricter length filters added later
evidence_records.Language: English-language Malaysian news (paper does not fully characterize multilingual coverage)
evidence_records.Sensitive-data status: public news about refugees, a vulnerable population; representational risks discussed only indirectly
evidence_records.Exact model/version: GPT-3.5-Turbo and Ada embedding model; snapshot IDs not reported
evidence_records.Prompting strategy: initial concise theme prompt; error-driven Socratic relevance/context/valence steps; JSON outputs; semantically matched cluster-code summaries as few-shot exemplars
evidence_records.Fine-tuning or adaptation: no weight tuning; prompts revised using human-review errors
evidence_records.Agent roles: GPT summarizes, codes and produces exemplar themes; embeddings/clustering retrieve examples
evidence_records.Human role: three reviewers independently rate codes, keep diaries, discuss disagreements, define error modes, revise the workflow and establish consensus reference labels
evidence_records.Generated outputs: relevance decision, specific theme, attitude holder, target and hostile/sympathetic valence
evidence_records.Evidence/provenance mechanism: review sheets include article URL/full text/title/summary/passage/code/cluster; final prompts retain the focal passage and matched examples
evidence_records.Baselines: initial one-pass prompt versus final Socratic/few-shot workflow; no independent non-LLM model baseline
evidence_records.Number of runs or seeds: two evaluated workflow iterations on the same 414-passage sample; no stochastic seeds
evidence_records.Automatic metrics: accuracy, precision, recall, F1, negative predictive value, Kendall's tau-b and exact confidence intervals
evidence_records.Human-evaluation design: three independent reviewers assess a fixed 414-passage sample, discuss disagreements and produce consensus; 153 model-irrelevant passages receive additional review
evidence_records.Number and expertise of evaluators: three human reviewers; domain/method expertise not fully specified

evidence_records.Reproducibility resources: Multimedia Appendix 1 contains prompts and Jupyter Notebook code; data are not public
evidence_records.Author-reported limitations: 2.6% truncation; one-label ground truth oversimplifies multi-issue complaints; human subjectivity; 2021/COVID context; class imbalance; pretrained models and undisclosed training/model details; language variation; no conventional ML/BERT comparator
evidence_records.Additional validity concerns: Supplying true category when predicting severity leaks ground-truth information into that field. The 15-topic 'thematic analysis' has no human comparison or grounding evaluation, and fieldwise raw accuracy is misleading under imbalance, as the low harm/severity kappas show.
evidence_records.Relationship to prior papers: uses established HCAT(GP) taxonomy and its human training; distinct from earlier Lee et al. ChatGPT complaint/thematic work
evidence_records.Relevance to the proposed ARR project: Strongly supports multi-field, chance-corrected reporting and expert double coding; also shows ARR must prohibit label leakage and separately validate generated themes rather than borrowing credibility from fixed-field results.

evidence_records.Title: Codebook Reduction and Saturation: Novel observations on Inductive Thematic Saturation for Large Language Models and initial coding in Thematic Analysis
evidence_records.Authors: Stefano De Paoli; Walter Stan Mathis
evidence_records.Publication history notes: arXiv v1; manuscript explicitly labels itself a draft that may contain errors
evidence_records.Citation count, source, and retrieval da: not collected; official arXiv full text inspected 2026-08-24
evidence_records.Relationship/dependence family: De Paoli–Mathis inductive thematic saturation series
evidence_records.Research objective: Characterize run/order variability in LLM initial coding and compare a zero-shot duplicate-reduction prompt with a DSPy-compiled reducer for an inductive thematic saturation ratio.
evidence_records.Claimed qualitative methodology: inductive thematic analysis and inductive thematic saturation
evidence_records.Actual operationalized methodology: GPT-3.5-Turbo-16k independently generates up to 15 code-description-quote triples per interview; a second LLM stage reduces duplicates either with a zero-shot prompt or a DSPy ChainOfThought prompt compiled from labeled code pairs; unique/total code ratio is treated as ITS and compared across repeated runs and interview sequences.
evidence_records.Inductive, deductive, or hybrid: inductive initial coding followed by learned/few-shot semantic duplicate classification
evidence_records.Dataset name: UK NHS trial-transparency interview dataset from De Vito et al. (2023)
evidence_records.Public or restricted data: source interview dataset cited with UK Data Service DOI; exact reuse package for this experiment not separately deposited
evidence_records.Number of participants: 12 interviewees

evidence_records.Document length: full interview passed one at a time; lengths not reported
evidence_records.Sensitive-data status: health-services professional interviews; secondary data, sensitivity handling not reported
evidence_records.Exact model/version: GPT-3.5-Turbo-16k
evidence_records.Prompting strategy: temperature 0; zero-shot initial-coding Prompt_1; zero-shot duplicate reducer Prompt_2; DSPy ChainOfThought/RandomSearch compiled reducer using demonstrations
evidence_records.Fine-tuning or adaptation: DSPy prompt compilation from 198 code-pair examples (99 different and 99 synthetic similar pairs manually adjusted), drawn from four open datasets with an 80/20 split; no weight fine-tuning

evidence_records.Human role: authors design prompts, construct and manually adjust training pairs, select the ITS formulation, and interpret semantic-similarity matrices; no independent human validation of final codebooks
evidence_records.Unit of analysis: interview for initial coding; code-description pair for duplicate reduction
evidence_records.Generated outputs: initial codes with descriptions and quotations, reduced cumulative unique codebooks, ITS ratios and semantic-similarity matrices
evidence_records.Evidence/provenance mechanism: initial codes retain representative quotations, but reduced-code provenance and source-level traceability are not fully evaluated
evidence_records.Baselines: zero-shot Prompt_2 reducer versus DSPy-compiled reducer; repeated same-sequence and alternative-sequence analyses
evidence_records.Number of runs or seeds: 7 repetitions of sequence 1 plus 6 interview sequences; random seeds not reported
evidence_records.Automatic metrics: unique/total code ITS ratio, range, coefficient of variation, linear fits and all-MiniLM-L6-v2 cosine-similarity matrices
evidence_records.Human-evaluation design: none reported for code validity, duplicate decisions, or thematic adequacy
evidence_records.Number and expertise of evaluators: authors only; independent evaluators not reported
evidence_records.Inter-rater reliability: not reported
evidence_records.Statistical analysis: descriptive ranges and coefficients of variation; illustrative linear regression and semantic-similarity matrices
evidence_records.Principal results: Initial-code totals varied from 162 to 182 across repeated runs despite temperature 0. DSPy-reduced ITS was more stable than Prompt_2 (CoV 3.88% versus 23.34% across repeated runs; 2.79% versus 19.4% across sequences), yielding roughly 65–81 unique codes and ITS about .40–.43.
evidence_records.Efficiency or cost results: DSPy described as more complex, technically demanding and potentially more expensive; no measured time or cost
evidence_records.Ethics and privacy treatment: not reported for this secondary analysis
evidence_records.Reproducibility resources: verbatim core prompts and the compiled DSPy prompt are included in the appendix; source dataset DOI cited; executable code and full outputs not reported
evidence_records.Author-reported limitations: draft status; DSPy complexity/cost and programming skill; training examples were partly synthetic and manually adjusted; different training datasets may change results
evidence_records.Additional validity concerns: ITS is a duplicate-rate statistic, not evidence of interpretive validity or theoretical/data saturation. The DSPy validation metric reportedly returned True on every training example, and no independent human judgment establishes that pair reductions or final codebooks are substantively correct.
evidence_records.Relationship to prior papers: Direct extension of De Paoli and Mathis (2024), arXiv:2411.12142, using the same ITS concept and authors' earlier LLM thematic-analysis procedures.
evidence_records.Relevance to the proposed ARR project: Supports explicit run-stability and codebook-reduction checks, but argues against using a stable ITS ratio as a stand-alone quality criterion without human semantic validation.

evidence_records.Publication type: published conference/book chapter with OSF preprint

evidence_records.Claimed qualitative methodology: end-to-end inductive thematic analysis following Braun and Clarke
evidence_records.Actual operationalized methodology: Amazon Bedrock custom orchestration decomposes an iTA process description into three independent coding agents, a consensus agent, and an automatically added translator when needed; outputs are compared response-by-response and theme-by-theme with the prior human analysis in a blinded external-expert template.
evidence_records.Inductive, deductive, or hybrid: inductive
evidence_records.Domain: artificial intelligence in education / computer-supported collaborative learning
evidence_records.Dataset name: CSCL scholars' definitions survey (Simon et al. prior work)
evidence_records.Public or restricted data: anonymous survey data and process prompt available on OSF
evidence_records.Number of documents: 184 substantive responses to four open-ended survey questions; 10 minimal responses excluded
evidence_records.Number of participants: survey respondent count is not clearly reconciled with response count in the inspected manuscript
evidence_records.Approximate corpus size: 184 analyzed responses; AI averaged 1.7 codes per response versus 2.5 for humans; about 5 AI themes versus 9.5 human themes per question
evidence_records.Language: primarily English with some French responses automatically translated
evidence_records.Sensitive-data status: survey consent covered full anonymous publication and reuse
evidence_records.Exact model/version: Claude 3.5 Sonnet via Amazon Bedrock; snapshot identifier and inference parameters not reported
evidence_records.Prompting strategy: high-level agentic process prompt; orchestrator task decomposition; three parallel coding calls followed by consensus/reconciliation and optional translation
evidence_records.Agent roles: orchestrator, three independent coding agents, consensus/reconciliation agent, and dynamically added translator
evidence_records.Human role: four domain experts produced the reference analysis; two external CSCL experts independently reviewed shuffled human/AI codes and themes; authors designed the benchmark rubric
evidence_records.Unit of analysis: individual survey response for codes; complete per-question code/thematic structures for themes
evidence_records.Generated outputs: codes, consensus codebook, themes, descriptions and final analysis narrative
evidence_records.Evidence/provenance mechanism: each response is paired with its human and AI code sets in the evaluation; themes list their constituent codes; full narrative provenance is weaker
evidence_records.Baselines: prior four-expert manual iTA of the same corpus
evidence_records.Number of runs or seeds: one reported MAS analysis; seeds and repeat runs not reported
evidence_records.Automatic metrics: descriptive proportions, average codes/themes and exact binomial tests for authorship identification
evidence_records.Human-evaluation design: two independent external PhD experts reviewed shuffled code sets for correctness, comparative preference and perceived source, then themes for clarity, representativeness, relevance, relatedness and source
evidence_records.Number and expertise of evaluators: four CSCL experts in the manual benchmark; two external PhD experts in CSCL with more than five years' experience
evidence_records.Inter-rater reliability: manual benchmark Krippendorff's alpha=.934; no inter-rater coefficient reported for the two external evaluators, whose judgments diverged substantially
evidence_records.Statistical analysis: descriptive percentages and exact binomial tests for selected authorship-identification results
evidence_records.Principal results: AI codes were individually judged appropriate in 91% of cases versus 81% for human codes, but evaluator 1 preferred human code sets for questions 1/2/4 (87%/71%/56%) while evaluator 2 usually judged both good (90%/92%/88%). Experts jointly found only 3 of 22 proposed related-theme pairs; the AI final report lacked a comprehensive narrative.
evidence_records.Efficiency or cost results: automation and translation described as reducing tedious work; no measured time or API cost
evidence_records.Ethics and privacy treatment: prior survey obtained consent for anonymous publication/reuse; model-provider privacy, IRB and data-transfer controls not reported

evidence_records.Author-reported limitations: single domain-specific dataset; need broader tests; parameters and agent prompts could be optimized
evidence_records.Additional validity concerns: Only two external evaluators produced sharply different comparative judgments, yet no reliability statistic is reported. evidence_records.Relationship to prior papers: Uses the same CSCL corpus and prior manual analysis as Simon et al.; uses the authors' earlier Claude 3.5 Sonnet MAS architecture, making it a dependent evaluation rather than an independent replication.
evidence_records.Relevance to the proposed ARR project: Strongly motivates blinded, code- and theme-level human evaluation plus narrative-quality assessment; the evaluator divergence and absent reruns argue for more reviewers and explicit plurality handling.

evidence_records.Relationship/dependence family: Sterna/Moskalewicz human phenomenology reference study plus 2026 LLM comparative reanalysis
evidence_records.Research objective: Test whether persona-prompted frontier LLMs can reproduce, complement or challenge a human phenomenological thematic analysis of clinical life-story interviews.
evidence_records.Claimed qualitative methodology: phenomenologically informed inductive thematic analysis / computational phenomenology
evidence_records.Actual operationalized methodology: GPT-4o, Gemini 2.5 Pro and Claude 4 Opus each perform three persona-prompted thematic analyses and synthesize them; internal experts map overlap and verify omitted themes against raw data, two blinded external experts rate human/model outputs on eight validity dimensions, embeddings compare semantics/style, and 115 lay raters assess isolated theme titles/descriptions.
evidence_records.Inductive, deductive, or hybrid: hybrid: inductive analysis constrained by a named investigator persona, prior meta-synthesis, textbook method, demographics and research questions
evidence_records.Dataset name: 24 Polish inpatient BPD life-story interviews from the authors' prior reference study
evidence_records.Public or restricted data: raw clinical transcripts not reported as public; prompts and derived outputs included in appendices/supplement
evidence_records.Number of participants: 24 clinical interview participants plus 4 expert judges and 115 Prolific public evaluators
evidence_records.Approximate corpus size: more than 150,000 words; 12 human themes, 5 GPT themes, 7 Gemini themes and 11 Claude themes
evidence_records.Language: Polish source interviews; manuscript does not clearly state whether all model inputs remained Polish
evidence_records.Sensitive-data status: highly sensitive mental-health narratives, anonymized before external-model analysis
evidence_records.Model family: OpenAI GPT; Google Gemini; Anthropic Claude
evidence_records.Exact model/version: GPT-4o; Gemini 2.5 Pro; Claude 4 Opus, described as August 2025 state of the art; default hyperparameters
evidence_records.Prompting strategy: investigator-persona simulation plus CO-STAR context/objective/style/tone/audience/response; prior meta-synthesis, textbook method, demographics and research questions; three analyses per model followed by synthesis
evidence_records.Fine-tuning or adaptation: none; in-context persona and domain/method conditioning
evidence_records.Agent roles: each model acts as a simulated primary investigator and thematic analyst; final within-model synthesis combines three iterations
evidence_records.Human role: two original-study experts map semantic/thematic overlap and verify novel themes; two independent external experts read raw data and blindly score all outputs; 115 public raters judge isolated themes
evidence_records.Unit of analysis: complete corpus for model analysis; themes/theme descriptions for expert, embedding and public evaluation
evidence_records.Generated outputs: themes and descriptions, within-model syntheses, overlap mappings, validity scores, embeddings and public authorship/content judgments
evidence_records.Evidence/provenance mechanism: experts verify outputs directly against the full raw corpus and prompts are reproduced; models produce thematic syntheses rather than a fully auditable segment-to-code ledger
evidence_records.Baselines: published human phenomenological analysis of the same corpus; cross-model comparison; blinded expert and public judgments
evidence_records.Number of runs or seeds: three analysis rounds per model followed by one synthesis; UMAP random_state=42; default model sampling parameters
evidence_records.Automatic metrics: semantic-overlap percentage, Jaccard coefficient, Qwen3-Embedding-8B cosine similarity, StyleDistance cosine similarity and UMAP
evidence_records.Human-evaluation design: two internal experts conduct non-blinded overlap/omission checks; two external experts blinded to source read all raw data and rate eight qualitative-validity dimensions; 115 Prolific raters judge shuffled isolated themes without raw data
evidence_records.Number and expertise of evaluators: two original clinical/phenomenology investigators; two external clinical/phenomenology experts; 115 nonexpert Prolific participants
evidence_records.Inter-rater reliability: Krippendorff alpha: human=.55, GPT=.69, Gemini=.84, Claude=.81 for four expert raters
evidence_records.Statistical analysis: Kruskal–Wallis tests with Dunn–Bonferroni post hoc comparisons, correlations/elasticity analyses, embedding cosine comparisons and UMAP
evidence_records.Principal results: Semantic overlap with the human interpretation was GPT 0%, Gemini 42% and Claude 58%; Jaccard was .21/.27/.28. Each model surfaced one author-verified omitted theme. External-expert mean validity was human 4.56, Gemini 4.21, Claude 3.68 and GPT 2.65; human and Gemini did not differ significantly. Public theme-title match favored Claude 4.17 and Gemini 4.06 over human 3.95/GPT 3.68, but public raters lacked raw data.
evidence_records.Efficiency or cost results: no analysis time or API cost; authors infer fewer words may achieve near-human ratings, but this is not a workflow-efficiency study
evidence_records.Ethics and privacy treatment: reference protocol approved KB-367/23 with consent; transcripts anonymized; Prolific participants consented; closed models received clinical narratives, and authors recommend local open models for optimal deployment
evidence_records.Reproducibility resources: verbatim prompting protocol and generated themes in appendices; named embedding models and UMAP settings; raw clinical data and execution code not reported as public
evidence_records.Author-reported limitations: only two external experts; public raters lacked raw data and expertise; results depend on prompting; output stability varied; closed-model safety risks; models produced thematic constellations rather than integrated phenomenological structures
evidence_records.Additional validity concerns: The abstract's claim that all models 'proved' capacity to mitigate human bias overstates one author-verified omitted theme per model. Verbosity correlated with expert scores, and three within-model runs are collapsed into a synthesis rather than reported as a stability distribution.
evidence_records.Relationship to prior papers: Direct reanalysis of the authors' prior human BPD phenomenology study; not an independent dataset or human benchmark.
evidence_records.Relevance to the proposed ARR project: Materially strengthens the case for raw-data-blinded specialist evaluation, multiple model families and verbosity controls; supports AI as a contrastive second reading, not proof of bias mitigation.

evidence_records.Authors: Elias Balt; Salim Salmi; Sandjai Bhulai; Stefan Vrinzen; Merijn Eikelenboom; Renske Gilissen; Daan Creemers; Arne Popma; Saskia Mérelle

evidence_records.Relationship/dependence family: psychosocial-autopsy Llama 3 deductive-coding evaluation
evidence_records.Research objective: Evaluate whether a locally hosted few-shot LLM can deductively code and summarize sensitive psychosocial-autopsy interviews with sufficient agreement and usable source-grounded summaries.
evidence_records.Claimed qualitative methodology: deductive qualitative coding and summarization
evidence_records.Actual operationalized methodology: Llama 3 70B classifies code applicability to segments, applies overlapping sliding windows to full transcripts, and summarizes positive windows for predefined codes; model labels are compared with researcher coding and two researchers qualitatively rate the summaries.
evidence_records.Inductive, deductive, or hybrid: deductive model coding with human review and proposed subsequent human inductive analysis

evidence_records.Public or restricted data: restricted; potential access only under MREC criteria and reasonable request
evidence_records.Number of participants: bereaved respondents represented in 38 interviews; exact number of unique respondents not separately reported in the inspected text
evidence_records.Approximate corpus size: 2,666 researcher-coded fragments; 1,254 LLM summaries qualitatively assessed; up to 30,000 words per interview
evidence_records.Document length: full interviews up to 30,000 words; model windows up to 300 words with overlap 75
evidence_records.Sensitive-data status: highly sensitive and potentially identifying suicide-bereavement interviews
evidence_records.Exact model/version: Meta-Llama-3-70B-Instruct, locally hosted via Hugging Face; 8,192-token context
evidence_records.Prompting strategy: few-shot binary classification and code-focused summarization; preliminary synthetic-data work and one transcript used for prompt engineering; one positive and one negative example per code removed from evaluation

evidence_records.Agent roles: binary code classifier, sliding-window labeler and source-referenced summarizer
evidence_records.Human role: researchers create and consensus-resolve the reference coding, engineer prompts/examples, and independently rate summaries before discussion
evidence_records.Unit of analysis: coded fragment for binary classification; overlapping 300-word transcript window for full-corpus application; code-specific summary
evidence_records.Generated outputs: binary code labels, code frequencies and source-referenced summaries
evidence_records.Evidence/provenance mechanism: summaries point back to original data/code locations, enabling human verification; restricted source data limit external audit
evidence_records.Baselines: manual coding by two independent researchers with third-researcher consensus
evidence_records.Number of runs or seeds: one main model run per task; no repeat seeds reported
evidence_records.Automatic metrics: sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, Cohen's kappa and code-frequency ratios
evidence_records.Human-evaluation design: two researchers independently rate each summary good/adequate/poor and analyze error themes, then resolve interpretations
evidence_records.Number and expertise of evaluators: two qualitative researchers plus a third consensus researcher for the manual corpus; two researchers for summary-quality review
evidence_records.Inter-rater reliability: binary model–researcher Cohen's kappa=.68; no reliability coefficient reported for good/adequate/poor summary ratings
evidence_records.Statistical analysis: descriptive accuracy, sensitivity/specificity, kappa, frequency ratios and qualitative error analysis
evidence_records.Principal results: Binary classification accuracy=.84 (SD=.09), kappa=.68; sliding-window transcript classification accuracy=.67. About 80% of summaries were good/adequate, but 19.7% contained unsolicited elaboration, 3.0% omitted crucial information and 1.3% hallucinated.
evidence_records.Efficiency or cost results: model took about 5 hours per interview versus about 4 human coding hours, but processed all 38 over 8 days versus a four-month human project calendar; proposed speedups were not tested

evidence_records.Reproducibility resources: publisher supplementary material and exact open model identifier; data restricted; executable code and complete prompts not clearly deposited
evidence_records.Author-reported limitations: corpus too small for training/test examples; 8,192-token context required windows that disrupted chronology; Dutch-only dataset; post-coding interpretation/time outside scope
evidence_records.Additional validity concerns: The same research context shapes reference coding and output review; summary-rating reliability is absent. Calendar-time comparison is not equivalent to labor time, and the unoptimized model was slower per interview than a human.

evidence_records.Relevance to the proposed ARR project: A high-value benchmark for sensitive local deployment, source references and structured error audits; shows that good aggregate accuracy can coexist with chronology failures and clinically consequential hallucinations.

evidence_records.Title: Efficiency with Rigor! A Trustworthy LLM-powered Workflow for Qualitative Data Analysis
evidence_records.Authors: Jie Gao; Zhiyao Shu; Shun Yi Yeo; Alok Prakash; Chien-Ming Huang; Mark Dredze; Ziang Xiao
evidence_records.Peer-reviewed status: not peer reviewed / venue not verified
evidence_records.Publication history notes: arXiv v3 dated 26 October 2025; ACM template still contains placeholder conference acronym, 2018 date and XXXXX DOI, so it must not be represented as an accepted archival paper
evidence_records.Citation count, source, and retrieval da: not collected; official arXiv full text inspected 2026-08-24
evidence_records.Relationship/dependence family: MindCoder human-in-the-loop qualitative-analysis system
evidence_records.Research objective: Design and evaluate a workflow that automates descriptive QDA stages while exposing reasoning and supporting analyst intervention, reflection and auditable codebooks.
evidence_records.Claimed qualitative methodology: human-centered, trustworthy thematic analysis / qualitative data analysis
evidence_records.Actual operationalized methodology: A GPT-5 web application chains raw text to open codes, subthemes, themes, findings and a theme map, with self-critique and user editing. Eight formative interviews derive requirements; a 12-person Latin-square comparison against Atlas.ti AI Coding and a blinded two-expert review assess experience/output quality; a separate six-dataset technical test uses lexical Jaccard coverage.
evidence_records.Inductive, deductive, or hybrid: primarily inductive; one participant demonstrates deductive use through research questions/predefined themes
evidence_records.Domain: HCI and general qualitative research tooling
evidence_records.Dataset name: six technical-evaluation text sets plus two public interview datasets on software quality and qualitative-data teaching
evidence_records.Public or restricted data: technical and study datasets described as supplementary/public; participant-study recordings not public
evidence_records.Number of documents: 72 technical-evaluation documents (12 each across six types); four roughly 1,000-word interview excerpts used across two user-study tasks
evidence_records.Number of participants: 8 formative QDA practitioners; 12 user-study analysts; 2 external evaluators
evidence_records.Approximate corpus size: technical documents 2,000–4,000 words each; each user-study dataset consisted of two approximately 1,000-word interviews
evidence_records.Document length: 2,000–4,000 words in technical test; about 2,000 words per user-study dataset
evidence_records.Sensitive-data status: public/non-sensitive task datasets; human-study recordings collected with consent
evidence_records.Exact model/version: GPT-5 via API with reasoning effort set to minimal; Atlas.ti baseline uses an undisclosed OpenAI model
evidence_records.Prompting strategy: four-stage prompt chain with about 1,000 instruction words per stage; user-defined code counts and prompts; self-critique, verification and JSON-constrained outputs; full prompt about 6,000 words in appendix/supplement
evidence_records.Agent roles: mechanical open coding, clustering, theme naming, quote preservation, self-critique, findings summary and DOT theme-map generation
evidence_records.Human role: analysts choose scope/specificity, inspect raw text and rationales, edit/regenerate codes and themes, prompt, memo and retain interpretive responsibility; authors/thematic analysts study use; external evaluators score outputs
evidence_records.Unit of analysis: text chunk, code, subtheme, theme and analyst interaction trajectory
evidence_records.Generated outputs: open codes tied to exact chunks, subthemes, themes, self-critiques, rationales, key findings, theme maps, memos, prompt history and final codebook trajectory
evidence_records.Evidence/provenance mechanism: exact original chunks are retained under codes; users can reopen source text; prompts, changes, memos and trajectories are exported
evidence_records.Baselines: Atlas.ti AI Coding in a counterbalanced within-subject comparison
evidence_records.Number of runs or seeds: technical reasoning chain repeated five times per dataset; user tasks one run per participant/tool; seeds not reported
evidence_records.Automatic metrics: word-set Jaccard coverage from text to codes
evidence_records.Human-evaluation design: 12 analysts use both systems on different datasets and complete Likert/think-aloud/interviews; two source-blinded external evaluators independently rate 24 codebooks on six questions spanning Lincoln–Guba trustworthiness dimensions
evidence_records.Number and expertise of evaluators: 12 analysts (4 expert, 6 intermediate, 2 novice self-reports); external E1 psychology PhD student with 4 years QDA, E2 data-science undergraduate with about 2 years QDA
evidence_records.Inter-rater reliability: not reported for external evaluators; user-interview analysis used first-author coding, second-author review/consensus and team member checking
evidence_records.Statistical analysis: paired t tests for external 10-point ratings; user Likert t tests were nonsignificant and reported descriptively
evidence_records.Principal results: Technical text-to-code lexical Jaccard averaged 89.6% (meeting transcripts 66.3%). User Likert differences were nonsignificant; MindCoder had higher descriptive agreement for flexibility/reflexivity/modification/ transparency, but Atlas.ti for efficiency and source engagement. Two experts rated MindCoder higher on all six questions (paired t, all p<.01), while noting redundancy, over-conceptualization and hierarchy errors.
evidence_records.Efficiency or cost results: Atlas.ti was perceived faster (9 versus 7 agreeing); GPT-5 latency hindered some users; generation took about 15 minutes for more than 10,000 words and no cost accounting was reported
evidence_records.Ethics and privacy treatment: institutional IRB approval reported for formative and user studies; participant consent/recording described; model-provider data handling and exact protocol identifiers not reported
evidence_records.Reproducibility resources: full prompts and technical dataset described in appendix/supplement plus Atlas.ti demo link; no verified public source-code repository or fixed model snapshot
evidence_records.Author-reported limitations: eight formative participants mainly positivist; 12-person study; only Atlas.ti baseline and both use OpenAI models; expert evaluation preliminary; GPT-5 latency; other trustworthiness/triangulation strategies untested
evidence_records.Additional validity concerns: Word-overlap Jaccard is incorrectly treated as content stability/trustworthiness and evaluates only text-to-code, not interpretive stages.
